backgrounds.desc:
You once walked the halls of an arcane academy, filling notebooks with formulas, diagrams and half-understood theory. Whether through failed exams, a scandal you'd rather not discuss, or simply running out of coin for tuition, you left before earning your mantle.

You know just enough magic to be dangerous and just enough theory to argue with real mages. Some dropouts carry a grudge against the masters who turned them away. Others still hope to prove they belonged there all along.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

feats.d: You still know a few people at your old academy, like a sympathetic tutor, a librarian or a fellow dropout. You can call on them for rumors, access to a library, or an introduction to a mage, though they may want a favor in return.

backgrounds.desc:
You bear a curse. Perhaps a witch spoke it over your cradle, perhaps you took something from a tomb that should have stayed buried, or perhaps it runs in your blood and has followed your family for generations. Whatever its source, it marks you in ways others can feel: candles gutter when you pass, animals shy away, and misfortune seems to gather wherever you linger.

You've learned to live with the whispers, the nightmares and the strange mark on your skin that never fades. Some of the accursed hide what they are. Others hunt for the one who cursed them, or for any power strong enough to break it, before it finally claims them.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice (an old or forbidden tongue you somehow understand)

gear.n: Tattered journal recording every sign of your curse

feats.d: People who bear their own curses, hauntings or brushes with the unnatural sense something familiar in you, and will confide in you when they won't speak to anyone else. Superstitious common folk, however, often keep their distance, make warding signs as you pass, or ask you to leave town.

backgrounds.desc:
You were raised or trained within the walls of a temple, tending its candles, reciting its rites and serving the faithful who came seeking comfort. You know the hymns, the holy days and the proper words for blessings, burials and oaths.

Whether you left to spread your faith, to answer a calling you couldn't ignore, or because you began to question what you'd been taught, the temple's teachings still shape how you see the world.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

feats.d: Temples and shrines of your faith recognize you as one of their own. You and your companions can find modest food and lodging there, and the clergy will share what they know about local troubles.

backgrounds.desc:
You spent your youth bent over a writing desk, copying ledgers, letters, contracts and old texts for a scholar, temple or guild. Your hand is steady, your letters are clean, and you've read far more than anyone meant you to, from forgotten histories to secrets scrawled in the margins.

Perhaps your master died, perhaps you copied something you shouldn't have, or perhaps you simply grew tired of writing about the world instead of seeing it. Either way, you set down the quill and stepped out to find stories of your own.
backgrounds.langs: Two additional languages of your choice

feats.d: Scriptoriums, archives and record halls recognize the marks of your training. You can gain entry to look through records, deeds and old texts that are closed to the public, as long as you treat them with care and don't take anything away.

backgrounds.desc:
You made your living on the open road, waiting in the treeline for merchants, pilgrims and anyone careless enough to travel without guards. Maybe you rode with a crew that answered to a ruthless captain, or maybe you worked alone, taking only what you needed to survive.

Whether you were driven to it by hunger, greed or a lord's cruelty, you know how to set an ambush, how to make a threat sound like a promise, and how to vanish before the patrols arrive. The roads remember you, even if you'd rather they didn't.

feats.d: You know the hidden signs bandits carve and scratch along the roads: marks for safe camps, guarded routes, easy targets and places to avoid. You can read these marks wherever you travel, and leave your own for those who know how to look.

backgrounds.desc:
You made your coin bringing people in, whether they were thieves, deserters, murderers or simply someone who owed the wrong person money. You learned to read a trail, question a tavern full of liars, and tell the difference between a frightened fugitive and a dangerous one.

Some bounty hunters follow a strict code and only take honest contracts. Others will hunt anyone if the price is right. Either way, you know that everyone runs eventually, and everyone leaves something behind.

feats.d: You know how bounties work: who posts them, where they're kept, and who pays out. In any town with a watch, magistrate or guild hall, you can learn who currently has a price on their head and what it's worth, and you can claim rewards without being turned away as a common thug.

backgrounds.desc:
You spent years on the trade roads with merchant caravans, loading crates, driving pack animals, mending harnesses and standing watch through long nights at camp. You've crossed deserts, mountain passes and border towns, and you've seen how much of the realm runs on the goods carried by people like you.

Perhaps you traveled with the Gold Dwarf trade clans, or with a human merchant house. Either way, you know the roads, the rest stops and the price of everything, and you've learned that the most dangerous part of any journey is usually the people waiting along it.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

feats.d: Merchant caravans recognize a fellow road hand. You can usually find work with a caravan in exchange for safe passage and meals for yourself and a few companions. Caravan crews will share news about the roads ahead, such as bandit activity, closed passes and which towns pay best.

backgrounds.desc:
You've spent your life measuring the world and putting it on paper. You've traced coastlines from the decks of ships, sketched mountain passes by firelight, and crawled through ruined halls with a lantern and a measuring cord, marking every turn so the next explorer wouldn't get lost.

Guilds, nobles and treasure-seekers paid well for accurate maps, and you learned that a good map is worth more than a sword in the wrong tunnel. Now you're heading into places no one has charted, to fill in the empty spaces yourself.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

feats.d: You know the trade in maps. In any sizable town, you can find someone who buys, sells or trades maps, and you can tell a real one from a forgery. Explorers, guilds and treasure-seekers may offer you commissions to chart new ground, which can be a steady source of work and rumors.

backgrounds.desc:
You've sold miracle cures that were only colored water, deeds to land that didn't exist, and noble titles you made up on the spot. You've worn a dozen names and told a hundred stories, and you've learned that people will believe almost anything if it's what they want to hear.

Maybe a con went wrong and you had to leave town in a hurry, or maybe you've decided to turn your talents toward bigger prizes. Either way, somewhere out there are people who'd very much like a word with whichever version of you robbed them.

gear.n: 5 stoppered vials of colored water labeled as miracle cures

feats.d: You can recognize fellow con artists by their patter and tricks, and they recognize you. In most towns, you can find someone in the trade who'll share gossip about easy marks, local authorities and which cons have already been run. Be careful, though: somewhere out there are people you've swindled who still remember your face.

backgrounds.desc:
You carried messages, packages and sealed letters across the city for merchants, guilds and anyone willing to pay. You learned every alley, rooftop, canal bridge and back stair, and you could cross the city faster than a carriage, slipping through crowds and over walls when the streets were too slow.

Couriers see everything and are noticed by no one. You've delivered love letters, threats, bribes and confessions, and you've learned that knowing who sends what to whom is a kind of power. Now you've traded the city's streets for longer roads.

feats.d: In any city, you can quickly learn its streets and shortcuts and find nearly any address, shop or person. Local runners and messengers will carry a message across the city for you for a few coppers, and they'll pass along gossip about who has been sending messages to whom.

backgrounds.desc:
You spent your life in the halls of power, though not always as one of the powerful. Perhaps you were a lord's advisor, a herald, a lady-in-waiting or simply a well-connected attendant. You learned to read a room, flatter the right person and smile at your enemies while they smiled back.

Court life taught you that words are sharper than swords, and that every favor has a price. Whether you fell out of favor, fled a scandal or were sent away on some delicate errand, you carry the manners and the cunning of the court with you.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

feats.d: You understand how noble courts work: their customs, rivalries and who really holds the power. You can usually arrange an audience with minor nobles or officials, and you hear the gossip that moves through palaces and manor houses before it reaches the streets.

backgrounds.desc:
You were raised in a secretive cult, or drawn into one when you were young and desperate. You chanted its prayers, kept its secrets and watched its rituals in the dark, believing for a time that you were part of something greater.

Then something broke the spell, whether a ritual that went too far, an order you couldn't follow or a truth you were never meant to see. You ran, and you've been running ever since. You still know their signs and their songs, and you suspect they haven't stopped looking for you.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice (learned from the cult's rites)

feats.d: You recognize the hidden signs, symbols and recruiting methods that secret cults use. You can often tell when a cult is active in an area and where its members might gather. Your old cult still searches for you, and its agents may turn up when you least expect them.

backgrounds.desc:
You once marched under a banner, drilled in formation and slept in the mud with your company. Then, at some point, you threw down your colors and walked away. Maybe you refused an order you couldn't stomach, maybe you saw a battle you knew was already lost, or maybe you were simply tired of dying for someone else's war.

Whatever the reason, the army calls it desertion, and the punishment is rarely kind. You've learned to keep your head down, avoid patrols and never stay too long in one place, but the habits of a soldier haven't left you.

gear.n: Soldier's uniform with the insignia torn off

feats.d: You know how armies work: their camps, patrols, signals and supply routes. You can often find other deserters and disillusioned soldiers who'll quietly share food, shelter or information. But your old army hasn't forgotten you, and anyone loyal to your former banner may recognize you for what you are.

backgrounds.desc:
You made your living in the shallow ruins and forgotten tunnels that lie beneath the realm, places where treasure-seekers go in and don't always come out. You've crept past collapsed halls, marked safe paths in chalk, and learned the hard way which doors should stay closed.

Delving was never glamorous. It was cramped, cold and dangerous, and most of what you found was rust and bones. But every so often the dark gave something back, and now you're ready to go deeper than you've ever gone before.

feats.d: Every town near a dungeon has a tavern or lodge where delvers gather, and you know how to find it. There you can hire or join a crew, trade rumors about newly opened ruins, and buy rough maps of the upper levels from those who made it back.

backgrounds.desc:
You carried out the final sentences of lords, magistrates and city courts. You stood on the scaffold before silent crowds, hooded or bare-faced, and did the work that others were glad to leave to someone else. You learned the anatomy of a clean end, and you learned to live with the stares that followed you through the streets.

Perhaps you executed someone you came to believe was innocent, perhaps your lord fell and took your position with them, or perhaps you simply couldn't lift the axe again. Whatever happened, people still remember your face, and few of them remember it fondly.

gear.n: Sealed writ of office from the court you served

feats.d: Jailers, guards and officers of the law treat you as one of their own. You can usually gain access to prisons and holding cells to speak with prisoners, and officials will share what they know about criminals and recent sentences. Common folk, however, tend to avoid you, and the families of those you executed may not have forgiven you.

backgrounds.desc:
You were cast out of the place you once called home, whether a clan, temple, city or kingdom. Maybe you broke a sacred law, took the blame for someone else's crime, backed the wrong side in a struggle for power, or simply said something that couldn't be taken back.

Now you wander lands that aren't your own, carrying the customs, the memories and the language of a home you can't return to. Some exiles want only to forget. Others spend every waking day planning their return.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice (from your homeland)

feats.d: In most large cities you can find others cast out from your homeland, living together in quiet communities. They'll offer you shelter, news from home and a sympathetic ear. But returning to your homeland means risking arrest or worse, and those who exiled you may still be watching.

backgrounds.desc:
You grew up working the land, rising before dawn to tend fields, mend fences, haul water and drive stubborn animals to pasture. The work was hard and the seasons were harsher, but it gave you a strong back, steady hands and a plain, honest way of seeing the world.

Maybe a bad harvest drove you off the farm, maybe raiders burned it down, or maybe you simply looked at the road leading out of the village and wondered where it went. Either way, you've traded the plow for the open road, but you still know the value of a hard day's work and a hot meal.

feats.d: Farmers and country folk see you as one of their own. In rural areas, you can usually find a meal and a dry place to sleep in a barn or farmhouse in exchange for a day's work. Country folk will tell you about the troubles they'd never mention to outsiders, like missing livestock, strange lights in the woods or a neighbor who's been acting odd.

backgrounds.desc:
You ran the quiet back room where stolen goods changed hands. Thieves brought you jewels, silverware and the occasional priceless heirloom, and you paid them a fraction of what it was worth before selling it on to buyers who never asked where it came from. You learned to judge a gem by its weight and a client by their nerves.

Maybe the watch finally caught up with your shop, maybe a deal went bad with the wrong people, or maybe you bought something you never should have touched. Whatever the reason, you've closed up shop and taken your keen eye for value on the road.

gear.n: Ledger written in your own code

feats.d: You know how to find the black market in any town. You can locate buyers for stolen, unusual or questionable goods, and sellers of things that can't be bought openly. Black-market contacts will also tell you what's been stolen recently and who's looking to buy, though they'll always take their cut.

backgrounds.desc:
You came from humble beginnings, but when danger came to your village, you were the one who stood up to it. Maybe you drove off a band of raiders, slew a beast that had been taking livestock, or defied a cruel lord's tax collectors in front of the whole town square. Whatever you did, the people haven't forgotten.

Your story is told around hearths and sung in taverns, and it grows a little grander with each telling. Now you've set out to see if you can live up to the legend, or to find out whether you were ever really a hero at all.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

feats.d: In your home region, your deed is sung in taverns and told around hearths. Common folk there will hide you, feed you and help you, as long as you don't betray their trust. Farther away your story is less known, but now and then a bard or traveler has heard some version of it, usually exaggerated.

backgrounds.desc:
You grew up in the heat and noise of a smithy, working the bellows, hauling ore and hammering out nails, hinges and horseshoes until your arms ached. Over the years your master trusted you with finer work, like blades, tools and armor fittings, and you learned to tell good metal from bad by its ring under the hammer.

Maybe you trained in a Black Iron fortress, a Mountain Dwarf hall or a simple village forge. Either way, you've left the anvil to see the world, and perhaps to find the rare ores and legendary techniques you've only heard about from old smiths' stories.

feats.d: Smiths recognize a fellow forge worker by your calloused hands and burn scars. In most towns you can use a smithy's forge in exchange for a day's labor, and smiths will tell you about local mines, rare metals and anyone who has ordered unusual weapons or armor lately.

backgrounds.desc:
You lived by the roll of the dice and the turn of a card. Smoky back rooms, riverboat tables and noble card parties were your hunting grounds, and you learned to read a bluff in the twitch of a lip and to slip away before a losing streak turned violent.

Fortune has carried you to great heights and dropped you into deep holes more times than you can count. Now you're betting on the biggest game of all, adventure, where the stakes are life and death and the payout could be a fortune.

feats.d: Gambling dens and card tables welcome you in every town, and you can always find a game. Gamblers talk when they're winning and talk more when they're losing, so you hear rumors, secrets and loose talk that never reach the streets. Somewhere out there, though, someone may still be holding your markers.

backgrounds.desc:
You earned your place in a craft guild through years of apprenticeship, careful work and a masterpiece judged by the guild's elders. Whether you're a smith, tailor, alchemist, woodworker or jeweler, your guild's seal on your work means quality, and your name is written in the guild's rolls.

Guild membership brings privileges, connections and protection, but also dues, politics and obligations. Maybe you've left to find rare materials for your craft, to escape guild politics, or to build a reputation that reaches beyond the city walls.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

gear.n: Set of tools for your chosen trade
Letter of standing from your guild

feats.d: Guild halls of your trade recognize your seal and your standing. In any town with a hall, you can find lodging among fellow members, rent time at their workstations, and call on the guild to speak for you in trade disputes or minor legal trouble. In return, the guild expects you to pay your dues and occasionally take on work in its name.

backgrounds.desc:
You learned your trade in a cramped workshop that smelled of oil, brimstone and hot brass, perhaps under a Gnomish craftsman, perhaps in a Gold Dwarf trading house that dealt in firearms. You spent years filing tiny springs, fitting locks and triggers, and measuring powder by the grain, learning that one careless mistake could cost a hand or a life.

Firearms are rare, expensive and feared, and few people truly understand how they work. You do, or at least you understand enough to know how much you've yet to learn. Now you've set out to find rare materials, new designs, or simply a chance to see what your craft can really do.

gear.n: Set of fine files and tweezers

feats.d: You are one of the few who has caught glimpses of firearm blueprints and their closely guarded secrets. You learn the following crafting recipes: Gnomish Pistol, Dwarven Musket, Silver Shot.

Gunsmiths, tinkers and the Gold Dwarf trade houses that deal in firearms recognize you as one of the trade. You can find where firearms and their ammunition are made or sold, even when they aren't sold openly, and craftsmen will share news of new designs, rare parts and who has been buying guns lately.

backgrounds.desc:
You never set foot in an academy. Your magic came in scraps: a few words learned from a wandering spellcaster, a battered spellbook bought from a peddler, charms and folk magic passed down from a village wise-woman. You learned by trial, error and the occasional singed eyebrow.

Trained mages may sneer at your methods, but your magic is practical, earthy and stubborn, built for mending fences, warding off pests and surviving in places where no scholar would set foot. What you lack in polish, you make up for in grit and creativity.

gear.n: Battered secondhand spellbook with half its pages missing

feats.d: You learn the following crafting recipes: Bitterthorn Draft, Minor Silverskin Potion, Minor Resistance Tonic.

Rural folk often trust a hedge mage more than a robed academy wizard. In villages and farmsteads, people will come to you for help with small magical troubles, like curdled milk, strange lights or a cursed well, and in return they'll offer food, shelter and local gossip.

backgrounds.desc:
You stand to inherit something of great value: a title, a parcel of land, a merchant fortune or the leadership of a proud family. Unfortunately, someone else wants it too. Perhaps a scheming relative, a rival house, or a usurper has pushed you out, and your claim is worth little unless you can survive long enough to press it.

You were raised with tutors, manners and expectations, but you've had to leave comfort behind. Whether you're gathering allies, proving yourself worthy, or simply staying out of reach of assassins, you carry your family's name and its burdens with you.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

feats.d: Your family name still carries weight. Old retainers, loyal servants and those who owe your family favors may quietly help you, offering shelter, information or a hidden route out of town. Your rivals also know your name, though, and agents of the house that wants your inheritance may be looking for you.

backgrounds.desc:
You spent years in fields, forests and marshes gathering roots, leaves, flowers and fungi, learning which ones soothe a fever, which ones stop bleeding and which ones can stop a heart. You know plants by their smell, their bark and the way they grow, and you trust nature's remedies far more than any priest's prayers.

Villagers once came to you for poultices and teas, and the occasional desperate patient came for something stronger. Now you travel in search of rare plants that grow only in dangerous places, ones whispered about in old herb-lore but seldom seen.

feats.d: You learn the following crafting recipes: Bitterthorn Draft, Minor Silverskin Potion, Minor Resistance Tonic.

You know where useful plants grow and when they're in season. Local healers, midwives and herb-sellers will trade knowledge and supplies with you, and they'll tell you about rare plants growing nearby, along with what dangers guard them.

backgrounds.desc:
For years you lived apart from the world in a mountain cave, a forest hut, a ruined chapel or a lonely stretch of moor. You might have gone seeking enlightenment or penance, or you might have been hiding from your past. Silence taught you patience, self-reliance and a way of seeing things that others often miss.

Something has drawn you back among people: a vision, a question that solitude couldn't answer, or a danger you saw coming that the world must be warned about. You return with simple needs, odd habits and a mind that has spent a long time in its own company.

gear.n: Journal of your thoughts and observations from your years alone

feats.d: Your old hermitage still stands in a remote place only you know how to find, whether a cave, hut or ruin. You and your companions can retreat there to hide, rest or store belongings, safe from all but the most determined pursuers. You can also recognize other recluses and wanderers of the wild, who will share shelter and quiet news with a kindred spirit.

backgrounds.desc:
You served a church as one of its hunters, rooting out heretics, cultists, demon-worshippers and practitioners of forbidden magic. You've interrogated the guilty and the innocent alike, burned profane books and walked into places where the faithful feared to go. Your faith is a weapon, and you were taught to wield it without mercy.

Perhaps you're still on a holy mission, hunting a heresy that slipped through your church's grasp. Or perhaps you've begun to doubt the orders you were given and the people you condemned. Either way, the darkness you've hunted hasn't forgotten you.

gear.n: Sealed writ of inquisition bearing your church's mark

feats.d: You learn the following crafting recipes: Silver Powder, Holy Water, Muting.

Temples and clergy of your faith recognize your authority, and the faithful are expected to cooperate with your investigations into heresy and dark magic. They'll answer your questions, open their records and point you toward suspicious activity. Common folk often fear you, however, and cults and dark practitioners will take a special interest in silencing an inquisitor.

backgrounds.desc:
You made your living solving problems others couldn't, like missing persons, stolen heirlooms, unexplained deaths and crimes the city watch had given up on. Maybe you wore the watch's badge, or maybe you worked privately for anyone who could pay. You learned to notice the scuff on a boot, the lie in a nervous smile and the detail that doesn't fit.

One case still haunts you, an answer you never found or a culprit who slipped away. You've taken to the road partly for work and partly because, somewhere out there, the trail of that case might finally lead somewhere.

gear.n: Set of common clothes with a long coat

feats.d: In any town, you know how to find the people who see everything: barkeeps, beggars, street sweepers and petty crooks. For a few coins or a favor, they'll tell you who's been seen where, what's been stolen and which rumors are worth chasing. City watchmen also tend to treat you as a useful professional rather than a nuisance.

backgrounds.desc:
You were knighted once, or trained to be, and swore oaths of courage, protection and honor. But you serve no lord's court. Instead you ride, or more often walk, from place to place, bound to a cause of your own: defending the helpless, hunting a great evil, fulfilling a vow made at a deathbed, or seeking redemption for a past failure.

Your armor may be dented and your surcoat faded, but your oath still burns bright. Some see you as a relic of a nobler age, others as a fool chasing legends. You simply see a road, a wrong to right, and the next town that needs a sword.

feats.d: Your knightly bearing and oath are recognized wherever chivalry is honored. Common folk in trouble will seek you out for help, and lords and ladies who respect the old codes will offer you hospitality for a night. But you're expected to live up to your oath, and breaking it in front of witnesses will quickly ruin your reputation.

backgrounds.desc:
You spent your days deep underground, swinging a pick by lamplight, hauling carts of ore and listening to the groan of timber supports holding back the weight of the mountain. Maybe you worked the dwarven halls, the iron seams beneath the Ash Fields, or a rough human mine where the pay was poor and the ceiling was worse.

You've seen tunnels collapse, gas flare and things crawl out of the dark that no miner ever wanted to find. You know rock, ore and the dark better than most, and you've decided that if you're going to risk your life underground, you might as well go looking for treasure instead of iron.

gear.n: 10 iron pitons and a small hammer

feats.d: Mining towns and dig camps welcome you as one of their own, and you can find work, shelter and a hot meal among them. Miners will tell you about old shafts, collapsed tunnels and anything strange that's been found, or heard, in the deep places.

backgrounds.desc:
When something with too many teeth started taking livestock, children or travelers, people sent for someone like you. You've tracked wolves the size of horses, burned nests of giant spiders and waited through freezing nights for something to come out of the dark. You know that every beast leaves signs, and every beast has a weakness.

Some hunt for coin, some for glory and some because a monster once took everything from them. Your trophies, scars and hard-won lore speak for themselves. Now you're after bigger prey, the kind that only lurks in the deepest places.

gear.n: Notebook of monster sketches and weaknesses

feats.d: Hunters, trappers and frightened villagers recognize your trophies and scars for what they are. In rural areas, people will bring you word of strange tracks, missing livestock and creatures that have been seen nearby, and they'll often offer food, shelter or payment if you deal with the problem.

backgrounds.desc:
You were born into a noble house, raised among banners, banquets and the endless business of land, titles and alliances. Tutors taught you history, etiquette, heraldry and the proper way to address a duke, and you grew up knowing that your family's name opened doors that stayed shut to everyone else.

But privilege comes with expectations. Perhaps you were sent out to prove yourself, to restore your house's fading honor, or to escape a marriage arranged for you. Or perhaps you simply wanted a life that was more than ceremony. You carry your family's name wherever you go, for better or worse.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

feats.d: Your house's crest is recognized among the nobility. Allied houses will offer you hospitality, and you can send letters home to request aid, though help may be slow to arrive and will come with expectations attached. Your family's rivals know your colors too, and their old grudges are now yours.

backgrounds.desc:
You were raised far from walls and roads, among nomadic clans, frontier settlers or a remote tribe at the edge of the known world. You learned to read the weather, follow game trails, find water in dry country and sleep under open skies in any season. Cities still feel loud, cramped and strange to you.

Something drew you away from the wilds, whether a duty to your people, a disaster that scattered them, or simple curiosity about the world beyond the horizon. You bring with you the instincts of the wild and a quiet confidence that you can survive where others would falter.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice (spoken by your people)

feats.d: Frontier settlers, nomadic clans and wilderness folk accept you as one of their own. They'll share their fires, their trails and news of the wild lands with you, including which passes are open, where herds are moving and which places are best avoided.

backgrounds.desc:
You've sung in smoky taverns, juggled in market squares, told stories by roadside fires and played for nobles who barely looked up from their wine. Whether you're a musician, actor, acrobat, storyteller or fire-eater, you know how to hold a crowd, and how to leave town quickly when a performance goes badly.

The stage taught you to read an audience, wear a mask and make people believe, if only for a moment. Now you're chasing a greater stage: adventures worth singing about, and perhaps a legend of your own.

gear.n: Lute (or another instrument of your choice)
Bundle of handbills advertising your act

feats.d: You can always find a stage, whether a tavern, a festival, a market square or a noble's feast. In exchange for a nightly performance, you can usually earn modest lodging and food for yourself, and audiences love to gossip with a performer after the show.

backgrounds.desc:
You're on a long journey toward a holy place: a distant temple, a saint's tomb, a sacred mountain or a shrine said to grant visions to the worthy. Perhaps you walk to fulfill a vow, to seek forgiveness, to find healing for someone you love, or simply because your faith called you to the road.

You've worn out more than one pair of boots, shared fires with strangers of every kind and learned that the journey changes you as much as the destination. Your road has now taken a detour into danger, but you trust it still leads where you need to go.

feats.d: Along sacred roads, shrines, waystations and pilgrim hostels will offer you a simple meal and a place to sleep. Fellow pilgrims share news of the road and of the holy sites ahead. Even some bandits leave pilgrims alone out of superstition, though not all of them.

backgrounds.desc:
You fought for money and the roar of the crowd, in fighting pits dug beneath taverns, chalk circles in back alleys and grand arenas where nobles placed bets from shaded boxes. You've faced brawlers, beasts and trained gladiators, armed with whatever the organizers handed you, whether a net, a spear or just your fists.

Maybe you won your freedom, maybe you fled a pit master who claimed you were his property, or maybe you simply decided that if you're going to bleed, you'd rather bleed for treasure. The crowd still chants your fighting name in your dreams.

feats.d: In any large town, you can find the local fighting pits and arenas, and you can always earn a bout and a purse there. Pit masters, bookmakers and regular crowds know the circuit and its fighters, and they'll trade gossip with you. Some of your old opponents may still hold a grudge, though.

backgrounds.desc:
You've lost your home, whether to war, plague, famine, a lord's cruel decree or a disaster that left nothing standing. You fled with whatever you could carry and joined the long, desperate columns of people searching for somewhere safe. Along the way you learned to make do with nothing, to read strangers quickly and to survive when the world seemed determined not to let you.

Perhaps you're searching for family scattered in the chaos, perhaps you've sworn to return and rebuild, or perhaps you've finally stopped looking back. Whatever drives you, you've already survived the worst the world can do, and that makes you harder to break.

gear.n: Bundle holding the few belongings you saved

feats.d: Those who have also lost their homes recognize you as one of their own. In refugee camps, charity houses and poor quarters, you can find a place to sleep and a share of what little food there is, and fellow refugees will pass along news of the troubles that displaced you and of loved ones still missing.

backgrounds.desc:
You've devoted your life to the pursuit of knowledge, spending years among dusty archives, crumbling scrolls and the debates of learned colleagues. Whether your passion is ancient history, the stars, forgotten languages, strange beasts or the nature of magic itself, you know more about your chosen field than nearly anyone alive.

But books can only take you so far. The answers you seek lie in lost ruins, sealed vaults and places no scholar has dared to go. Now you've set out to find them yourself, armed with your mind, your notes and a growing suspicion that the truth is stranger than any book suggests.
backgrounds.langs: Two additional languages of your choice

gear.n: 2 well-worn books on your field of study
Unanswered letter from a fellow scholar

feats.d: You keep up letters with scholars, librarians and experts across the realm. Given time, often days or weeks, you can send a question about your field and receive an answer, a rumor or a lead on where the answer might be found. Your colleagues will expect the same favor in return.

backgrounds.desc:
You've worked the decks of merchant cogs, fishing boats, river barges or perhaps a ship with a darker trade. You climbed the rigging in storms, hauled nets until your hands bled and learned a hundred knots, a dozen shanties and every sailor's superstition. The sea gave you a strong back, a steady balance and very little patience for landlubbers.

Maybe your ship sank, maybe your captain cheated the crew, or maybe you simply grew tired of seeing ports only from the docks. Now you've traded the open sea for open roads and dark tunnels, though you still miss the salt air.

feats.d: In any port or river town, dockworkers and sailors recognize one of their own. You can find work on a ship or arrange cheap passage for yourself and your companions, and dockside taverns will tell you which ships are coming and going, what cargo they carry and which captains can't be trusted.

backgrounds.desc:
You survived on what others threw away. You picked through rubbish heaps, battlefields, flooded cellars and abandoned houses, salvaging scrap metal, broken tools and the occasional forgotten treasure. You learned that almost anything can be fixed, sold or made into something useful, if you know how to look.

People called you a rag-picker, a gutter-diver or worse, but you know the value of things better than most merchants. Now you've set your sights on the richest scrap heaps of all: ruins and dungeons where entire fortunes lie abandoned in the dark.

feats.d: You know the junk dealers, rag-pickers and scrap merchants of every town. They'll buy your salvage when no respectable merchant will, and tell you where things have recently been dumped, abandoned or left unguarded, along with any odd finds that have turned up.

backgrounds.desc:
You've fought for lords, merchants, rebels and anyone else who could pay. Battles, caravan guard duty, border skirmishes and the occasional job you'd rather not talk about have all been part of the work. Loyalty, for a sellsword, lasts exactly as long as the coin does, and you've learned to collect your pay before the fighting starts.

Maybe your mercenary company broke apart, maybe your last employer refused to pay, or maybe you've grown tired of fighting other people's wars. Now you're looking for work where the reward is better than a soldier's wage, and dungeons pay in gold.

gear.n: One weapon from your chosen category worth no more than 15 (G)
Contract from your last employer that was never fully paid

feats.d: You know how mercenary work is found and paid. In any town of some size, you can find recruiters, caravan masters or nobles hiring blades, and you can tell an honest contract from a trap. Old comrades from your former company may turn up now and then, as allies or as rivals on the other side of a contract.

backgrounds.desc:
You moved goods that weren't supposed to move: untaxed wine, forbidden books, stolen relics, Gold Dwarf firearms and the occasional passenger who needed to leave town unseen. You knew the hidden coves, the forgotten tunnels beneath the city walls and which customs officers could be bribed, and which ones would get you hanged.

Maybe a shipment went wrong, maybe a rival crew sold you out, or maybe the watch finally learned your face. You've slipped away with your skills and a few dangerous contacts, and you're ready to take on cargo of a different kind: treasure hauled out of the deep places of the world.

gear.n: Small Box with a False Bottom

feats.d: You know how smugglers move goods and people unseen. In most towns and ports, you can find hidden coves, forgotten tunnels or bribable gates, and smugglers willing to move you, your companions or your cargo past the authorities, for a fee.

backgrounds.desc:
You were the only one who came back. Maybe it was an expedition into a ruin that swallowed your whole company, a caravan lost in a storm, or a ship that broke apart on the rocks and left you alone on a strange shore. You remember fragments: screams in the dark, cold water and a face you can't quite place. But you don't remember how you survived, and that troubles you more than anything.

People look at you differently now. Some think you're lucky, some think you're cursed, and some quietly wonder what you did to be the one who lived. You've set out to find answers, to finish what your companions started, or simply to prove that you deserved to survive.

gear.n: Torn and salt-stained pack from your lost company

feats.d: Your story spreads ahead of you. Families of those who were lost, scholars, treasure-seekers and the curious will seek you out, offering food, shelter or coin for your account of what happened. Now and then, a fragment of your lost memory returns at the DM's discretion, often when you return to a place connected to your tragedy.

backgrounds.desc:
You gathered secrets for a crown, a noble house, a guild or a rival power. You've worn false names, forged friendships with people you were sent to betray, and slipped stolen letters into hidden pockets at grand balls and back-alley meetings alike. You learned that the most dangerous weapon in the realm is information in the right hands.

Maybe your cover was blown, maybe your masters cast you aside, or maybe you learned a secret so dangerous that both sides now want you silenced. Whatever happened, you still think like a spy: you watch the exits, trust no one fully, and always have a story ready.
backgrounds.langs: One additional language of your choice

feats.d: You know how spy networks pass messages: hidden drops, chalk marks and coded signals. In most cities, you can find a way to contact your old network, or another one, to trade information or send secret messages. But spies always want something in return, and agents of the powers you've crossed may be watching for your signals too.

backgrounds.desc:
You served a knight, carrying their arms, polishing their armor, tending their horse and following them into tournaments and battles. You learned the code of chivalry by watching it lived, or broken, and you've dreamed of the day you'd earn your own spurs.

Perhaps your knight fell in battle, perhaps they sent you out to prove yourself, or perhaps you left after seeing a side of knighthood you couldn't stomach. Either way, you carry your knight's lessons with you, and you know how to keep a warrior and their gear in fighting shape.

gear.n: Kit for polishing armor and oiling leather
Letter of service signed by your knight

feats.d: Knights, knightly orders and their households recognize you as one in training. You can usually find a bed and a meal in a knight's hall or an order's chapterhouse, and knights will share news of tournaments, campaigns and quests seeking willing blades. Your former knight may still call on you for help, or vouch for you when it counts.

backgrounds.desc:
You grew up alone on the city streets, sleeping in doorways, under bridges and in forgotten corners of crowded slums. You learned to pick pockets, dodge the watch, find food where no one else would look and run before trouble caught up with you. Every alley was a hiding place and every rooftop a road.

The streets made you quick, clever and hard to fool, but they also taught you that no one looks out for you except yourself, and perhaps the other children who shared your scraps. Now you've found a way out of the gutter, and you don't intend to go back.

gear.n: Pouch of chalk for scratching street signs
Scrap of oilcloth you sleep under

feats.d: People of wealth and rank have spent their lives ignoring children like you, and you've learned to use it. When you're dressed in rags, guards, nobles and merchants rarely give you a second glance. You can loiter near market stalls, servants' doors and busy courtyards without drawing attention, so long as you don't give anyone a reason to look twice.

backgrounds.desc:
You ran an inn or tavern, pouring ale, cooking stew, breaking up fights and listening to every traveler who passed through your door. You've heard confessions, boasts, rumors and secrets, and you've learned to read a customer's mood before they've finished their first drink. Your tavern was the beating heart of its little corner of the world.

Maybe a rival bought you out, maybe the place burned down, or maybe the stories your customers told finally convinced you to go see the world for yourself. Your tavern may be behind you, but you still know how to keep a crowd fed, cheerful and talking.

gear.n: Club (your old "peacekeeper" from behind the bar)
Handwritten recipe for your house stew

feats.d: Your old tavern still stands, perhaps run by family, a trusted barkeep or a partner who owes you. Whenever you return, you and your companions have a warm bed, a hot meal and a safe place to rest, store belongings and receive messages. The regulars there are always eager to share the latest news and gossip.

backgrounds.desc:
You made your fortune, or tried to, by breaking into the resting places of the ancient dead. Crypts of forgotten kings, sealed barrows and buried temples were your hunting grounds, and you learned to spot a pressure plate, read faded warnings in dead languages and pry gold from a skeleton's grip without a second thought.

Some call you a grave robber, and the priests call you worse. But you know the dead have no use for treasure, and the deeper the tomb, the greater the prize. You've survived traps, collapses and things that should have stayed buried. Now you're ready for the deepest vaults of all.

gear.n: Set of fine brushes and probes

feats.d: You know the collectors, antiquities dealers and less scrupulous scholars who pay well for ancient relics and no questions asked. They'll buy what you dig up, trade rumors of unopened tombs, and sometimes hire you outright. Temples, tomb guardians and the descendants of the dead you've robbed, however, take a very dim view of your work.

backgrounds.desc:
You lived by snares, skins and patience, spending long seasons alone in the wilds setting lines, checking traps and hauling furs to distant trading posts. You learned the habits of every creature in your territory, where they drink, where they sleep and where they run when frightened, and you learned to move so quietly that they never knew you were there.

Maybe the fur trade dried up, maybe something in the woods began emptying your traps before you could, or maybe a long winter alone finally drove you to seek company. Whatever the reason, you've brought your quiet skills and keen eyes out of the wilds and into a far more dangerous kind of hunting ground.

gear.n: Bundle of furs ready for trade

feats.d: Trading posts, tanners and fur traders know you by name. They'll buy your pelts and hides at a fair price, extend you modest credit, and pass along news from other trappers about strange tracks, emptied traps and what's been stirring in the wilds.

backgrounds.desc:
You prepared the dead for their final rest, washing and dressing bodies, building coffins, digging graves and speaking the rites that send souls on their way. Death came to your door every day, and you learned to meet it calmly, with steady hands and a quiet respect that comforted the grieving.

You've also seen things most people never do: bodies that didn't rest easy, graves found empty, and deaths that were no accident. Perhaps one of those mysteries has drawn you out into the world, or perhaps you've decided it's time to deal with the dead before they come looking for the living.

gear.n: Small kit of embalming oils and linen wraps

feats.d: Gravediggers, mourners and cemetery keepers trust you as one of their own. You can learn who has died recently and how, read burial records, and hear rumors of disturbed graves, missing bodies and restless spirits. Grieving families will often turn to you for help when something about a death doesn't sit right.
